title: ARGUEMENT ARENA (DEBATE)
participants: 02 members per team and one team per institution.
rules:
1. Team Composition:
    • Two Teams: Each debate consists of two teams—one supporting the topic (For) and the other opposing it (Against).
  2. Topic and Preparation:
    • Debate Topic: Topics will be given 10 minutes in advance. Lots will be drawn for opponent selection and For/Against.
    • An elimination round will be conducted if the number of teams is odd.
    • For the elimination round, topics will be given on the spot, and participants must speak on the given topic for 2 minutes.
  3. Speaking Order and Time Limits:
    • Opening Statements:
      • For Team: 4 minutes to present their arguments.
      • Against Team: 4 minutes to present their counterarguments.
    • Response:

      The Response and Rebuttal Round will be an open-format segment lasting 8 minutes, where both teams may freely engage with and challenge each other’s opening statements.

      Participants are encouraged to present counterarguments, clarify positions, and respond directly to points raised by the opposing team.

    • Closing Statements:
      • Teams will be given 2 minutes each to present their closing statements.
  4. In Case of an Odd Number of Teams:

    A presentation round will be conducted in which all teams will present for 2 minutes each on the provided topics. The team with the least points will be eliminated.

  5. Conduct Rules:
    • Respect: Speakers must maintain respect for each other and avoid personal attacks or rude language.
    • No Interruptions: Team members should not interrupt the speaker except during the designated response time.
    • Fact-check: Use accurate and reliable information to support your argument.
  6. Scoring and Feedback:
    • Points: Judges will score based on the criteria above.
    • Tie-Breaker: If there is a tie, an additional round or question may be used to determine the winner.
    • Judge’s Decision: The decision of the judges is final and cannot be challenged.
  7. Penalties:
    • Time Overrun: Exceeding the time limit may result in point deductions.
    • Rule Violations: Breach of any rules may lead to penalties or disqualification.
judging:
• Content: Quality, relevance, and depth of the arguments. [10 Points]
  • Delivery: Clarity, confidence, and persuasiveness of the speech. [10 Points]
  • Rebuttal: Ability to effectively counter the opposing team’s points. [10 Points]
  • Team Coordination: How well the team members support each other and present a unified argument. [10 Points]
  • Structure: Logical flow and organization of the speech. [10 Points]
